name: Romanian Deadlift
runnerRationale: The hinge that builds hamstring and glute strength through length. Stronger hamstrings at long muscle lengths are what let the leg absorb landing forces stride after stride.

name: Single-Leg Deadlift
runnerRationale: Running is a series of single-leg landings. This trains the hinge and the frontal-plane hip control that keeps the pelvis level, on one leg at a time — and exposes side-to-side differences a barbell hides.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
runnerRationale: Loads hip extension with the knee bent and the joint kept shallow, so glute strength can be built without asking much of the knee. A useful main lift while deeper positions are still off the menu.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
runnerRationale: Low-load, low-risk single-leg hip extension. Often the first thing that can be trained hard again, and it keeps the glutes contributing while heavier work is still restricted.

name: Box Squat
runnerRationale: A squat where the box sets the depth, so range is a number you choose rather than a thing that happens. That makes it the squat variation to use while knee flexion is being reintroduced under load.

name: Back Squat
runnerRationale: The highest-yield bilateral leg strength builder once deep flexion under load is cleared. Strength here transfers to hill running and to holding form late in a race.

name: Goblet Squat
runnerRationale: A front-loaded squat that self-limits how much can be piled on. Good for grooving the pattern at moderate load once depth is available.

name: Dumbbell Split Squat
runnerRationale: Single-leg strength in a stable, non-pivoting stance. The split position loads one leg heavily without the bilateral load a barbell squat puts through the spine and both knees at once.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
runnerRationale: Concentric-dominant single-leg work whose difficulty scales with box height as well as load — two dials instead of one while range is being rebuilt. Closely mimics hill running mechanics.

name: Standing Calf Raise
runnerRationale: Straight-knee plantarflexion loads the gastrocnemius and the Achilles. The calf complex absorbs and returns more energy per stride than any other muscle group in running, and it is chronically undertrained.

name: Seated Single-Leg Calf Raise
runnerRationale: Bending the knee takes the gastrocnemius out of it and puts the work on the soleus, which carries the larger share of the load in distance running. The straight-knee version alone leaves this gap open.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
runnerRationale: Heavy eccentric hamstring loading. The best-evidenced single exercise for reducing hamstring strain injury, and it builds eccentric strength exactly where running demands it — late swing phase.

name: Lying Leg Curl
runnerRationale: Isolated knee flexion. Less specific than a hinge, but it loads the hamstring at short lengths that the RDL leaves out, and it is easy to control when other options are restricted.

name: Leg Extension
runnerRationale: Direct quadriceps loading with no hip contribution. Open-chain knee extension places shear through the joint that closed-chain work does not, which is why clearance for it is a separate question from clearance to squat.

name: Hip Abduction
runnerRationale: Weak hip abductors let the pelvis drop and the knee fall inward on each landing — the mechanism behind a large share of running knee and IT-band complaints. Loading them directly is the fix.

name: Banded Monster Walk
runnerRationale: Hip abduction under continuous tension while the foot is on the ground, which is closer to how the muscle actually works during running than a seated machine.

name: Pallof Press
runnerRationale: Anti-rotation. Running is a rotational sport the trunk spends its time resisting; training that resistance directly is more useful than training flexion.

name: Dead Bug
runnerRationale: Anti-extension with the spine supported. Keeps the ribcage stacked over the pelvis while the limbs move — the same job the trunk has for every stride of a long run.

name: Side Plank
runnerRationale: Lateral trunk endurance, trained as a hold. Pairs with hip abduction work against the same pelvic drop on landing.

name: Back Extension
runnerRationale: Posterior-chain endurance for the spinal erectors, which fatigue late in long runs and take posture with them when they go.
